steps.text: This alert shows svchost.exe opening lsass.exe, referencing the OTRF dataset SDWIN-201023023651. I need to figure out whether this reflects benign system behavior or something malicious by examining the relationship more closely.

arguments.reasoning: Read access mask and details of the svchost to LSASS handle access

steps.text: That PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION call tracing through lsm.dll's RPC looks benign — I should verify the source process has a legitimate path and parent before ruling it out entirely.

arguments.reasoning: Verify the svchost source process image path, command line, and user

steps.text: This looks benign — svchost running from system32 with standard access rights, and an lsm.dll call trace via RPC is normal behavior. I don't think I need to check the target further.

submission.reasoning: svchost.exe (C:\windows\system32\svchost.exe) on workstation5 opened lsass.exe 6 times between 06:36:43 and 06:36:44. The granted access was only 0x1000 (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), which cannot read LSASS memory. The call stack runs through RPCRT4 into lsm.dll, the Local Session Manager service, which matches normal session-management RPC handling. Nothing points to credential dumping: there is no PROCESS_VM_READ access, no unknown modules in the call trace, and the svchost image is in its normal system path. This is routine OS activity.
